bihar_raw_news.content: Museum Ranking 2026: Bihar museum secures top position in Asia, ranks 9th globally The ranking identifies 10 museums in Asia, with institutions from Japan, Malaysia, South Korea, Indonesia and India featuring on the list Join Our WhatsApp Channel Business Today Desk Updated Oct 28, 2026 3:00 AM IST Bihar Museum is the only Indian institution featured among the 100 museums selected worldwide The Bihar Museum in Patna has earned international recognition after securing the ninth position in the World’s 100 Best Museums 2026 list published by travel platform Worth a Journey. The museum has also been ranked the best in Asia, placing Bihar’s rich historical and cultural heritage in the global spotlight. Advertisement According to the ranking, Bihar Museum is the only Indian institution featured among the 100 museums selected worldwide. Its ninth-place finish puts it among some of the world’s most prominent cultural institutions, highlighting its role in preserving and showcasing India’s heritage. Read More READ THIS: No phone, no cars, almost no people. Here is why tourists are paying ₹1.06 lakh to visit this ‘Ghost Island Bihar museum among global leaders The 2026 list features museums dedicated to art, history, science, technology and open-air collections across different continents. Mexico City’s Museo Nacional de Antropología secured the first position, followed by Spain’s Museo del Prado in second place and Denmark’s Louisiana Museum of Modern Art in third. The State Hermitage Museum in Russia and Vienna’s Kunsthistorisches Museum also featured among the top 10 institutions. Bihar Museum’s inclusion in this group marks a significant achievement for India’s museum and cultural tourism sector. Advertisement The ranking identifies 10 museums in Asia, with institutions from Japan, Malaysia, South Korea, Indonesia and India featuring on the list. Bihar Museum emerged as the continent’s highest-ranked institution, ahead of other prominent Asian museums. Showcasing Bihar’s rich cultural heritage Established in Patna, Bihar Museum is a modern state museum that traces the region’s history from the Stone Age to contemporary times. Its collection includes ancient sculptures, coins, manuscripts, archaeological artefacts and regional folk art. The museum’s galleries are arranged chronologically, helping visitors understand Bihar’s historical development and cultural evolution. Its spacious premises, open courtyards and landscaped lawns complement the exhibitions. The museum also features a short film on history, making it an educational destination for students, researchers and tourists. Boost for Bihar’s tourism potential The international recognition could strengthen Patna’s position as a cultural tourism destination and encourage more domestic and international visitors to explore Bihar’s heritage. The ranking also highlights the growing importance of modern museums in presenting historical collections through engaging visitor experiences. The Bihar government has introduced a 100-point performance assessment index to evaluate banks operating in the state. IDFC FIRST Bank topped the ranking with 74 points. Key Points Performance Assessment Index: Banks have been classified into three zones based on their scores: Green Zone: Includes 11 banks scoring 50 or above. Yellow Zone: Comprises 7 banks. Red Zone: Contains several banks, including public sector banks. Annual Credit Plan 2026–27: Bihar has set a credit disbursement target of ₹4.95 lakh crore . By 30 th September 2026, banks had disbursed ₹1.89 lakh crore, achieving 38.25% of the target. Credit disbursement to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) reached ₹84,091 crore, while agricultural credit disbursement stood at ₹43,967 crore. Credit-Deposit Ratio (CDR): Bihar's CDR stood at 60.17% as of 30 th September 2026 . The state government urged banks to increase lending within the state, clear pending loan applications and improve credit access, particularly under the Kisan Credit Card and PM Vishwakarma schemes. Credit-Deposit Ratio The Credit-Deposit Ratio (CDR) is the ratio of a bank's total loans and advances to its total deposits, expressed as a percentage. It indicates the extent to which deposits mobilised by banks are converted into credit. Naz Ozair, an engineer from Muzaffarpur, Bihar, developed a patented technology to manufacture eco-friendly utensils from corn husks, promoting plastic alternatives and rural entrepreneurship. Key Points Innovation: Naz Ozair, a resident of Muradpur village, Kurhani block, Muzaffarpur, developed a technique to convert discarded corn husks into cups, plates, bowls, glasses, straws and bags. Startup: He established MNO Swadeshi India Pvt. Ltd. , which was incorporated on 5 th September, 2023, to manufacture these products. Environmental Significance: The innovation promotes agricultural-waste utilisation and offers alternatives to single-use plastics. Government Support: The Bihar government encourages rural innovations under the Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin) and Lohia Swachh Bihar Abhiyan . Single-Use Plastic SUPs are disposable plastic items designed to be used once or for a short period before being discarded or recycled. Examples: Packaging materials, bottles, polythene bags, coffee cups, cling film, trash bags and food packaging. From 1 st July 2022 , India prohibited 21 identified single-use plastic (SUP) items with low utility and high littering potential under the Plastic Waste Management Amendment Rules, 2021. Manufacturers, importers and brand owners are required to ensure the collection and recycling of post-consumer plastic waste. Implementation Challenges: Limited alternatives, high costs for MSMEs and the continued use of thin plastic carry bags hinder effective enforcement. national_raw_news.title: PM Modi says, India must embrace emerging technologies and lead world in creating them
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that India must innovate and lead the world in shaping the technologies of tomorrow. Speaking at the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave in New Delhi, Mr Modi said India must embrace the technologies of the future, innovate boldly and lead the world in creating them. He stressed that a Viksit Bharat will be built on strong foundations of scientific research, discoveries and the spirit of innovation. The Prime Minister stated that the nation is rapidly advancing its Fast Breeder Reactor technology. He highlighted that just a few months ago, the 500-Megawatt Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor successfully achieved first criticality. Mr Modi said that science truly succeeds when it steps out of the lab, improves the lives of common citizens, solves massive problems, and strengthens healthcare, agriculture, education, employment, and disaster resilience. He also highlighted that over the past year, the government has committed 12 thousand crore rupees to market-ready lab technologies, matched equally by 12 thousand crore rupees from private investors. He noted that annual patent filings have grown from fewer than 50,000 ten years ago to nearly 1.5 lakh last year, reflecting a deeper structural shift beyond mere numbers. Mr Modi said India aims to achieve self-reliance and build strength in critical technologies. He highlighted that the India of the 21st Century is moving ahead with a new mindset and newfound confidence. He stated that the goal is to create new technology for India, for the world, for today, and for the days to come. Meanwhile, Union Minister of State for Science and Technology Dr Jitendra Singh has said that India has established its position in science, innovation and technological capabilities, and the world is looking at the country with respect and admiration. He added that the international conference is witnessing enthusiastic participation, with thousands of experts and delegates joining the event on Indian soil. Prime Minister Modi also visited different sections of the exhibition and interacted with people. The exhibition includes around 150 deep-tech startup stalls, which will highlight technological developments and their potential applications across sectors. The three-day Conclave brings together leading scientists, researchers, academicians, policymakers, industry leaders, startups and international experts to deliberate on emerging technologies and India’s science, technology and innovation priorities. The deliberations will span 12 thematic areas, including artificial intelligence, biotechnology, advanced materials, manufacturing, healthcare, energy, climate and ocean sciences. Discussions will focus on research priorities, national capabilities and translating scientific advances into practical applications.

national_raw_news.title: India to bring further amendments to National Anti-Doping Act to introduce criminal provisions: S...
national_raw_news.content: Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Mansukh Mandaviya has said that India will bring further amendments to the National Anti-Doping Act to introduce criminal provisions. He said the move is aimed at strengthening action against doping violations, including those involving coaches and supply chain stakeholders. Dr Mandaviya made the announcement while chairing the third formal meeting of the COP10 Bureau and the fourth formal meeting of the Fund’s Approval Committee for 2026-27 under the UNESCO International Convention against Doping in Sport in New Delhi. The Minister said sporting excellence must be accompanied by integrity and that athletes should compete on the basis of talent, preparation and hard work, rather than prohibited substances or methods. Highlighting the country’s efforts to combat doping, Dr Mandaviya said India has strengthened its legal and institutional framework through the National Anti-Doping Act, 2022, and its 2025 Amendment, both of which came into force in July 2026. He said the government plans to bring another amendment in the next session of Parliament to introduce criminal provisions to deal more effectively with violations, including those involving coaches and stakeholders in the supply chain. Dr. Mandaviya said the National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA) conducted more than 7,000 tests during 2025-26 and organised over 350 education and awareness sessions, reaching approximately 27,000 participants. The agency has also focused on risk-based testing and intelligence-led investigations to strengthen its efforts against doping.

national_raw_news.title: UAE President honours FlyDubai pilot Captain Smit Machchhar with top civilian bravery award for s...
national_raw_news.content: UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan has conferred the First Class Order of Zayed II on the flydubai crew members, including Captain Smit Machchhar. The honour, one of the UAE’s top civilian awards, has been conferred in recognition of their courageous efforts to ensure the safety of passengers during an in-flight incident aboard FZ1073, travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv on September 30. The UAE President, in the presence of Vice President & Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, received the crew members. The leaders praised the crew’s courage and professionalism in ensuring the safety of passengers and securing the aircraft, affirming that protecting people’s safety and security remains a top priority for the UAE. The crew members expressed their gratitude to the UAE President and pride in receiving the honour, which reflects recognition of their service, dedication and commitment. The honours were presented by UAE Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence, Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, who commended the crew’s actions and sense of responsibility. The ceremony was also attended by Sheikh Theyab bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Deputy Chairman of the Presidential Court for Development and Fallen Heroes’ Affairs, and Sheikh Ahmed bin Saeed Al Maktoum, Chairman of Dubai Airports and Emirates Airline and Group, along with other senior officials. On September 30, Captain Smit Machchhar was attacked by his co-pilot while aboard flydubai flight FZ1073 enroute from Dubai to Tel Aviv. The crew, assisted by another pilot on board and passengers, intervened to bring the situation under control. The pilots regained control of the aircraft and diverted it to Tabuk in Saudi Arabia, where it landed safely. UAE investigations later revealed that the co-pilot had planned to seize the aircraft and carry out an attack at Tel Aviv airport.

national_raw_news.title: Exit polls show deadlock in Israeli Parliamentary elections, setting stage for coalition government
national_raw_news.content: The parliamentary election in Israel remained deadlocked, with exit polls from all three major television networks giving opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot’s bloc a narrow two-seat lead over Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s camp. The projections put Eisenkot’s bloc at 52 seats and Netanyahu’s Likud-led alliance at 50, leaving neither side with the 61 seats needed for a majority in the 120-member parliament – Knesset. The results could give Eisenkot the first chance to form a government, but his path to power remains uncertain. The remaining 18 seats were projected to go to Arab parties not aligned with either bloc, and Eisenkot has largely ruled out forming a government with them. Netanyahu, meanwhile, could remain caretaker prime minister if coalition talks fail. Israel’s Central Elections Committee said voter turnout reached 77.7%, the highest in more than two decades and around seven percentage points above the 2022 election. The vote was the first since the Hamas-led October 7, 2023, attacks and the ensuing wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran. Netanyahu has served as prime minister for nearly 19 of the past 30 years and has repeatedly survived political crises. His opponents removed him from office only once since 2009, but he returned to power 18 months later. With the latest exit polls showing a narrow advantage for Eisenkot’s bloc but no clear majority for either side, the final count and subsequent coalition negotiations will determine who can form Israel’s next government.

national_raw_news.content: The very severe cyclonic storm Arnab has commenced its landfall process along the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts near Kakinada. According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the landfall process started at 1:20 AM today. The crossing began earlier than originally expected due to the rapid movement of the storm. The storm hit the coast, packing sustained maximum wind speeds of 115-125 km per hour, with gusts reaching up to 140 km per hour. Heavy rainfall and strong winds have disrupted normal life across several coastal districts of Andhra Pradesh. In Puducherry, normal life has been affected in the coastal region of Yanam as cyclonic storm Arnab began making landfall near Kakinada in the early hours of this morning. Heavy rain and strong winds have lashed southern Odisha under the influence of cyclonic storm Arnab. Rain continues in Ganjam, Gajapati, Koraput, Malkangiri and Nabarangpur, with rainfall intensity likely to increase today. The IMD has issued a red warning for five districts and an orange warning for several other parts of the state. Odisha is maintaining heightened preparedness, with the Chief Minister scheduled to monitor the post-landfall situation from the Special Relief Commissioner’s office. Continuous rainfall since last night has affected Ranchi and several other parts of Jharkhand due to Cyclone Arnab. The Meteorological Department has issued an orange alert for heavy rainfall and strong winds. The West Bengal administration has stepped up precautionary measures in view of Cyclonic Storm Arnab. According to the Alipore Meteorological Office, scattered rainfall is likely in several districts of West Bengal today. Isolated spells of heavy rain are forecast in South 24 Parganas, East and West Midnapore, and Jhargram. Darjeeling and Jalpaiguri in North Bengal may also experience rainfall accompanied by gusty winds.

national_raw_news.content: Heavy rain and strong winds have lashed southern Odisha under the influence of cyclonic storm Arnab. Rain continues in Ganjam, Gajapati, Koraput, Malkangiri and Nabarangpur, with rainfall intensity likely to increase today. The IMD has issued a red warning for five districts and an orange warning for several other parts of the state. Odisha is maintaining heightened preparedness, with the Chief Minister scheduled to monitor the post-landfall situation from the Special Relief Commissioner’s office. Southern Odisha continues to experience heavy rain and strong winds under the influence of very severe cyclonic storm Arnab, which is crossing the Andhra Pradesh coast. According to the India Meteorological Department’s latest available landfall update, the storm was centred near the Andhra coast, close to Narsapur, after moving west-north-westwards. It is crossing the coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, close to south of Yanam, with sustained wind speeds of 125 to 135 kilometres per hour and gusts up to 145 kilometres per hour. In Odisha, Ganjam, Gajapati, Koraput, Malkangiri and Nabarangpur are among the districts facing severe weather. Gopalpur recorded the highest rainfall in the state over the last 24 hours, according to the available information. No casualties have been reported in Odisha so far. The state government is closely monitoring the situation, with Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi and the Revenue Minister scheduled to review post-landfall developments at the Special Relief Commissioner’s office. Authorities have shifted more than one lakh people living in vulnerable areas to safer locations. A number of trains have been cancelled, or routes have been diverted for today, while bus services to southern districts from other parts of the state have been completely suspended. Fishing activities remain suspended as the sea continues to be very rough.
